prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Reclaim the best measured ranking generator (xgboost, iteration 2's exact hyperparameters and scale_pos_weight 5.07, impute=none<path>=false so the trees split on NaN natively) and change exactly one thing: preprocessing gains missing_count=true. This is the run's first preprocessing-only transition, so the paired Δ against iteration 2 (balanced_accuracy 0.7585, roc_auc 0.8572, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7851) is attributable to that single aggregate column and nothing else. The column is the one thing a NaN-splitting tree cannot already express — its splits are per column, while missing_count aggregates across the 60 partially-missing columns (worst 0.785), so it stands in for how much of a respondent's questionnaire was completed, which in this file plausibly tracks wave<path> rather than a single field. Read balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut on the resulting row: if it stays inside 0.7851~0.7922 the ranking ceiling is confirmed and 0.8882 is unreachable on these columns, and the last iteration should be spent only on the operating point of this same ranking (cut_headroom on iteration 2 was 0.0266, so at most that much is buyable there).",
  "model_family": "gbdt",
  "candidate_models": [
    "xgboost"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "n_estimators": 800,
    "learning_rate": 0.04,
    "max_depth": 4,
    "min_child_weight": 10,
    "subsample": 0.8,
    "colsample_bytree": 0.6,
    "reg_lambda": 10.0,
    "reg_alpha": 1.0,
    "scale_pos_weight": 5.07,
    "early_stopping_rounds": 50
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "none",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": true
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Iteration 3 was mlp on median-imputed, scaled features with missing_count=true and no weight lever; this attempt abandons the neural family entirely and returns to xgboost. Against the best row (iteration 2) the only difference is preprocessing: missing_count goes false→true. Every hyperparameter, the imputation policy (none), scaling (false) and missing_indicator (false) are held identical to iteration 2, so this is a single-lever row — the first preprocessing-only transition in the history. It differs from iteration 2 by that added column and from iteration 3 by family, imputation, scaling and the presence of scale_pos_weight.",
  "rationale": "The bar 0.8882 sits 0.0960 above the best cut of every ranking measured so far (best_cut span across three families 0.7350~0.7922, width 0.0572), and cut_headroom on the best row was only 0.0266 against a 0.1297 shortfall — so the remaining distance is on the ranking axis, and no threshold or weight point can reach it. Iteration 3 demonstrated that spending an attempt on a fourth family off the list is not a plan that reaches the bar and, worse, moved several levers at once so nothing was attributable. With two iterations left the honest use of this one is to restore the highest measured ranking and isolate the single information lever never measured here: missing_count. Its value is genuinely unknown on this file — the ledger's prior measurements on a clinical sample gave it 0.0003 under a random split and it was never refitted under a contiguous one, so I am not citing a size, only noting it is the one column a NaN-splitting family cannot express and that the split here is stratified random, which would score a recording-regime signal as a gain. Cost is trivial (iteration 2 fit in 6.5 s of the 600 s budget, early stopping fired at 595 of 800 on 4,523 fit rows with 503 held back), so the risk is only the iteration itself. The decision rule is explicit: best_cut inside 0.7851~0.7922 confirms the ceiling and the run should report the bar as unreachable on these columns.",

  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 4
}
